craft_claim: Reflective passages must yield back to stimulus — scene, event, or a newly opened question — on a regular cadence, because sustained interiority without yield models rumination's escalation and starves the comprehension questions that hold readers; this tone therefore saturates by stalling rather than by intensity.

supporting_evidence.location: Cognitive Therapy and Research 27(3):247-259; longitudinal brooding/reflection results
supporting_evidence.note: Self-focused repetitive negative thinking (brooding) escalates distress over time while purposeful reflection does not — a dose pattern showing that inwardness without progress compounds rather than resolves; prose that models the same pattern invites reader fatigue by analogy.

Comprehension runs on generated why/how/what-next inferences; a text that suspends events without feeding questions leaves that machinery idle, and engagement depends on keeping questions open and progressively answered.

supporting_evidence.location: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology 79(5):701-721; transportation predictors
supporting_evidence.note: Transportation is fed by engagement with narrative events and imagery; consecutive interiority-only paragraphs lower event and imagery density and with it absorption.

counterevidence.note: No experiment located varies reflective-passage length against reader fatigue; all numeric thresholds derived from this claim are bounded writer-inference triangulated from adjacent findings, not measured saturation points for the tone.

scope: Reader-fatigue guidance for sustained reflective narration across forms; thresholds are explicitly heuristic and genre-conditional.
exceptions: Diary, letter, zuihitsu, and one-page essay forms license longer reflective runs by reader contract; there saturation shows as monotony of stance rather than as length.
At stakes-peaks the tone must yield entirely to scene or urgency per the taxonomy's dominance rule.
